_comment: Dialogue lines for Ono, the small companion who greets the student on the Hub screen. Each pool is an array of 'sequences' (an array of lines shown one at a time); Companion.gd picks one sequence at random depending on how far along the student's overall mastery is. Written warm and understated - never twee, never scored harshly.

early: Oh - hello. I didn't hear you come in.
It's a bit static-y out there. Every wave you clear puts a little more light back into things.
Somewhere out there, on a screen just like the one you're looking at now, this is a real exam. I know. Let's go gently.
Ten ideas, six more, and a few in te reo Māori. That's a lot to carry into a fight.
You don't have to carry all of it today. Just start the first wave.
mid: The light's holding a bit steadier now, between waves. That was you.
Keep going - not fast, just steady.
Error Prevention and Error Recovery still mix people up, you know.
Before the mistake, or after it. That's the whole difference. You'll get it.
late: It's brighter than when you found it. That wasn't luck - that was you sitting with the hard bits between waves.
Whatever room this understanding lives in on the actual exam day, I hope some of this stays with you.
You could stop here, if you wanted. It would still count.
Or you could run it again. Some things are worth knowing properly, not just well enough.
